newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products close mostly firm on soy gain.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products close mostly firm on soy gain.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures closed mostly firmer on gains in soybean futures, traders said.
Monday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook for normal to below normal temperatures in the U.S. Midwest September 22-26 boosted the market, they said.

Also USDA Monday said the U.S. soybean condition rating sagged slightly during the latest week and that as of Sunday, 17 percent of the crop was dropping leaves, well behind the average pace of 29 percent.
A rumor China was seeking 200,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans for October/November shipment and talk China was seeking soyoil probably from South America, also helped boost prices, the traders said.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 14,000 contracts, down from 21,599 Monday, according to the CBOT. Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, down from 25,735 Monday.
Soyoil futures closed 0.04 cent per lb higher to 0.07 lower, with September up 0.04 at 25.31 cents. Soymeal was unchanged to $2.50 per ton lower, with September up $2.50 at $273.80 a ton.
